title: SDE I (Python Developer)
description:
**SDE I**

**About the role**

We build low-latency, multi-tenant systems that admit user sessions, allocate compute capacity, and deliver

interactive realtime media at scale. As an SDE-1 you will help design, implement, and operate backend services

that sit on the critical path of session lifecycle — from authenticated API entry through resource assignment,

queueing under load, and clean teardown — with a strong focus on correctness, observability, and production

reliability.

**What you will work on**

• Build and evolve REST APIs for session creation, status, credential refresh, and teardown.

• Implement admission controls: rate limits, concurrency caps, and waiting queues when capacity is scarce.

• Contribute to worker-pool orchestration: registration, health-gated admission, reservation, assignment, and

fail-closed release.

• Work on realtime edge paths — WebSocket and/or RTC transports, timeouts, and client-facing connection

flows.

• Debug distributed failure modes: timeouts, races, idempotent webhooks, and multi-service state consistency.

• Improve tests, logging, and documentation so production behavior stays understandable.

**Technology stack**

Languages- Python

**Responsibilities**

• Ship well-scoped backend features with clear API contracts and error handling.

• Write correct async code against databases and Redis (transactions, locks, retries, idempotency).

• Investigate production issues using logs, metrics, and service contracts; propose durable fixes.

• Add automated tests for concurrency and failure edge cases.

• Participate in code review, CI, and safe Kubernetes rollouts.

**Requirements (must have)**

• Strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and system design basics.

• Proficiency in Python; comfort with async programming or clear ability to ramp quickly.

• Working knowledge of REST APIs, HTTP semantics, and JSON APIs.

• Solid SQL fundamentals; exposure to relational databases (PostgreSQL preferred).

• Understanding of concurrency: race conditions, locks, timeouts, retries, idempotency.

• Ability to read existing codebases, write clean PRs, and communicate trade-offs.

**Nice to have**

• Experience with FastAPI or similar Python web frameworks.

• Redis (queues, locks, caching) or other coordination primitives.

• WebSockets or realtime / media systems.

• Docker / Kubernetes; cloud exposure (Azure, AWS, or GCP).

• Auth patterns such as JWT and signed webhooks.

• Interest in observability: structured logs, tracing, latency and error SLIs.

title: Software Development Engineer 2 – Fulfilment
description:
**Software Development Engineer 2 – Fulfilment**

**About Urban Company**

Urban Company is Asia's largest tech-enabled home services marketplace, operating across India, UAE, Singapore, and Saudi Arabia. Customers use our platform to book a wide range of services — beauty and grooming, cleaning, plumbing, carpentry, appliance repair, painting, and more — delivered at home, at a time of their choosing. Behind this simple promise sits a deep technology stack that matches millions of customers with trained, background-verified service partners while guaranteeing a standardised, high-quality, and reliable experience every single time.

**About the Fulfilment Team**

The Fulfilment team sits at the heart of Urban Company's marketplace — we make sure every customer gets the right service, from the right partner, at the right time. We do this through three core charters:

- Planning & Shaping: Efficiently planning supply to meet forecasted customer demand, and intelligently shaping that demand to meet business goals.

- Capacity Management: Managing partner time and computing real-time availability of UC services for any given time slot, customer location, business category, and skill requirement.

- Allocation & Recovery: Assigning the most suitable partner for each job while maintaining fairness in partner earnings, and protecting customer experience in cases of no-shows, cancellations, or partner unavailability.

These are classic marketplace optimization problems — forecasting, matching, scheduling, and real-time recovery — solved at the scale of millions of monthly service requests.

**Job Description: SDE-2**

We are looking for experienced Software Development Engineers (SDE-2) to join our Fulfilment team. You will work on complex, high-impact engineering challenges — the systems you build directly determine whether a customer's booking is fulfilled seamlessly and whether a partner earns fairly. If you enjoy problems that blend distributed systems, optimization, and real-world operational constraints, this is the team for you.

**Responsibilities**

- Design and build scalable, high-performance, fault-tolerant systems and services that power supply planning, capacity, and allocation.

- Develop and optimize intelligent algorithms and ML/AI-driven solutions for demand forecasting, capacity planning, and partner–job matching.

- Own features end-to-end — from ideation and design to deployment, monitoring, and iteration across a modern tech stack.

- Raise the bar on the team's engineering practices: code quality, system architecture, observability, and operational excellence.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Analytics, and Data Science teams to translate business problems into robust technical solutions.

**What Are We Looking For?**

- Experience: 2–3 years of experience building large-scale backend applications or Products.

-Technical Strength: Strong foundation in Data Structures, Algorithms, OS, Networks, and Database fundamentals, with a good understanding of distributed systems, concurrency, caching, and scalable architectures.

- Backend Skills: Proficiency in at least one backend language (Node.js, Java, Go, or Python). Experience with databases (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL) and messaging systems like Kafka is a plus; exposure to cloud platforms and production observability is desirable.

- AI Fluency: Hands-on experience leveraging AI in day-to-day engineering — using AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Copilot, Cursor, Claude) to ship faster, and/or building with LLMs, ML models, or intelligent automation in production systems. Curiosity to apply.

- AI to real marketplace problems is a strong plus.

- Mindset: Bias for action, end-to-end ownership, and comfort with ambiguity.

- Team Player: Ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams and stakeholders.

**Why Join Us?**

- Work on marketplace-scale optimisation problems that few companies in the region get to solve.

- High ownership from day one — your systems ship to millions of users.

- A culture that rewards initiative, craftsmanship, and first-principles thinking.

description:

**Python & C++ Senior Software Engineer – Data Access (FIP)**
FactSet is seeking a highly skilled
**Senior Software Engineer**
to join our Data Access team — the single, powerful entry point to the FactSet Intelligence Platform (FIP). This is where every interaction begins: AI agents & tools, internal analytics, and client-facing APIs all connect through one unified endpoint and receive responses in a consistent, structured envelope enriched with provenance, source attribution, and entitlement transparency. Operating at the very front of FactSet's data ecosystem, you'll define this client-facing interface and orchestrate the systems behind it, delivering data with exceptional speed, security, reliability, and precision.
  
  
The platform handles immense volumes of low-latency requests, so strong engineering discipline is essential — you'll apply best practices in distributed systems, scalability, and performance to build infrastructure that is both resilient and efficient. It's a unique opportunity to shape a critical layer of FactSet's architecture, one that directly shapes the client’s experience and enables the next generation of intelligent applications. If you're passionate about building high-performance systems, simplifying complex data interactions, and making a measurable impact at scale, we'd love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Design, develop, and deploy the Data Access interface that defines how clients access data.
* Implement query patterns and APIs that balance flexibility, performance, and security.
* Enforce entitlements to ensure clients access only authorized data products.
* Leverage metrics and KPIs to optimize query execution, incorporating caching and performance strategies to meet client SLAs.
* Build observability into the layer — end-to-end request tracing, provenance, and source attribution surfaced in responses.
* Own Data Access products and features, driving bug fixes, performance enhancements, and scalability improvements.
* Collaborate with stakeholders and cross-functional teams to continuously improve development processes.
* Mentor junior engineers and contribute to technical design reviews and architecture decisions for the Data Access layer.
* Participate in a regional on-call rotation to support production system

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree or equivalent in Computer Science or related field.
* 5+ years of software engineering experience with a focus on API development, query systems, or data infrastructure.
* Strong proficiency in Python and C++, with experience building production-grade, client-facing systems.
* Solid understanding of OOP principles and software design patterns.
* Experience with API design and building orchestration layers across multiple backend systems.
* Proven ability to work independently and collaboratively, with experience leading technical initiatives.
* Passion for designing and implementing efficient, scalable, and maintainable software.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with multithreaded programming, low latency, and high-availability systems.
* Knowledge of query engine architecture, parsers, compilers and interpreters.
* Experience implementing caching strategies (Redis, Memcached) for query results and metadata.
* Experience with service-oriented architecture and microservices design.
* Understanding of distributed systems and handling failures gracefully across service boundaries.
* Experience working with large-scale data systems and balancing latency, throughput, and cost.
* Background with rate limiting, throttling, and client quota management.

**Company Overview**
FactSet (NYSE:FDS | NASDAQ:FDS) helps the financial community to see more, think bigger, and work better. Our digital platform and enterprise solutions deliver financial data, analytics, and open technology to more than 8,200 global clients, including over 200,000 individual users. Clients across the buy-side and sell-side, as well as wealth managers, private equity firms, and corporations, achieve more every day with our comprehensive and connected content, flexible next-generation workflow solutions, and client-centric specialized support. As a member of the S&P 500, we are committed to sustainable growth and have been recognized among the Best Places to Work in 2023 by Glassdoor as a Glassdoor Employees’ Choice Award winner. Learn more at www.factset.com and follow us on X and LinkedIn.

title: Builder Developer II
description:
**Job Description**
**The Builder-2 (Dev) Profile**
You are a full-stack agent engineer. You can take a complex business requirement and build the multi-step AI workflow that solves it, end to end, without someone breaking it down for you first.
  
  

* Core DNA
* AI-Native Workflow. You use AI to accelerate development, testing and documentation as a default, not an experiment. You have opinions about which tools earn their place.
* Agentic Implementation. You build, debug and deploy autonomous agents (LangGraph, AutoGen, Playwright-LLM hybrids) that navigate complex ERP schemas and long-running business logic.
* Legacy-to-Modern Bridge. You treat 20-year-old systems as puzzles for AI-driven modernization, not as someone else’s problem.
* Evidence Over Confidence. You don’t ship an agent because the demo went well. You ship it because you can show what it does on the edge cases — and you know your own error rate rather than claiming there isn’t one.
* What You Own

**Your agent.**
Design, build, debug, deploy, and keep running. Including the unglamorous parts: retries, state recovery, timeouts, what happens when the model is down.
  
  
**The evidence it works.**
Before you refactor an undocumented module, you capture what it currently does — characterization tests, real inputs, real outputs. After, you show the behaviour matches. Your Builder 3 sets the standard; meeting it is your job, not theirs.
  
  
**Your blast radius.**
You know exactly what your agent is permitted to touch, and you build so a wrong answer costs a review comment rather than a bad ledger entry.
  
  

* Your Elective Specialty (lean into one)
* The Agentic Architect (Systems) — you don’t just build APIs, you build tool-calling interfaces and state management for agentic graphs that survive long-running business processes.
* The UX/Interaction Builder (Product) — the chatbox is just the beginning. You build generative UIs and browser-use agents that navigate existing portals to get work done.
* The Data & Context Engineer (Data) — master of the RAG pipeline. Vector stores, chunking strategy, and knowledge graphs that teach the AI how a Purchase Order relates to a GL entry.
* The Reliability & Eval Engineer (QA) — you move the team from prompt vibes to prompt engineering. DSPy for programmatic optimization, red-teaming agents to pressure-test financial logic.
* The Infra & Agent-Ops Builder (DevOps) — you build the factory where agents live: tracing, logging and monitoring the thoughts of the AI.
* The Domain Logic Translator (Business) — you take 50 pages of accounting regulation and turn it into structured system prompts and agentic constraints.

**What You’ll Actually Do**

* Build execution agents. Move beyond RAG into action — agents that navigate an ERP schema, find a data discrepancy and propose the fix.
* Automate the untestable. Wrap legacy business logic in modern tests and documentation using AI, starting with the modules everyone else has avoided.
* Prove parity. Capture what the old code does before you replace it, and show the new path matches — on the boring cases and the fiscal-calendar, multi-currency, partial-shipment ones.
* Prompt engineering and evals. Use frameworks like DSPy to move from vibes-based prompting to programmatic, optimized instructions.
* Rapid prototyping. Turn a “what if” into a working AI-driven feature in days, not months.
* Fix your own agents in production. Read the traces, find why it went sideways, make it not happen again.

**What Good Looks Like**
*(Illustrative — real targets agreed with the hiring manager.)*

* 30 days: Shipped your first agentic workflow into a real environment, however small.
* 90 days: Owning a legacy module end to end — parity evidence, tests, deployment — with minimal supervision.
* 6 months: Other Builders are reusing patterns you built. You’re the person people ask about one thing in particular.

**The Stack**
Python, SQL (Postgres/SQL Server), TypeScript, OpenAI/Anthropic, agentic coding tools, LangChain/LangGraph, DSPy, pgvector/Qdrant, dbt, Apache Hop/Airflow, Docker, Playwright, Weights & Biases, OpenTelemetry, eval and tracing platforms (LangSmith / Langfuse / Braintrust or equivalent). And any other tool that helps us achieve greatness.
  
  
**Who You Are**

* You’ve shipped one. You have built at least one autonomous agent or complex LLM workflow that real people used for real work — not a weekend demo. You know how it failed, because it did.
* The early adopter. You were using GPT-3 before it was cool and had a local model running the week it leaked. More time on r/LocalLLaMA, GitHub Trending and AI Twitter than on LinkedIn.
* Agent-first thinker. You think in capabilities and failure modes, not functions.
* The manual-task hater. You have a physical reaction to repetitive work. If you do it twice, you’ve already started drafting the automation.
* Technically fearless. A 500-table undocumented legacy schema isn’t complexity, it’s a puzzle about to get solved. You aren’t intimidated by spaghetti code — you’re the one who brings the sauce.
* Rigor over hype. You love the new models and you still ask for the numbers. You know the difference between a cool demo and a production-grade agent handling financial data.

**Why Join Us**

* The Final Boss of complexity. ERPs are the ultimate challenge for AI. Automate a General Ledger or a global supply chain and you’ve mastered the hardest problem in software.
* Agentic autonomy. We don’t do tickets. We do missions. You’ll have real freedom over the models, frameworks and agent architectures you think will win.
* No red tape. If the agent works and the evals pass, we ship. No Change Management Committee — a “Does It Work?” policy.
* The Builder Tribe. You won’t be the only AI person in the room. You’ll be part of a small squad of people equally obsessed with moving faster, where your automation hacks are your biggest contribution rather than a hidden side project.

title: Builder Developer III
description:
**The Builder-3 Profile**
You are a systems engineer for non-deterministic systems. You are comfortable saying "no, not yet" to a working demo, and you can say exactly what would change your mind.
  
  

* Core DNA (shared foundation, at lead altitude)
* AI-Native Workflow. You don't just use AI tools fast — you set the squad's bar for what "fast and safe" looks like, and you remove the bottleneck when someone hits one.
* Agentic Architecture. You still build end-to-end agents yourself, and you do. But your leverage comes from designing the state management, tool interfaces and failure semantics that everyone else builds inside.
* Legacy-to-Modern Sequencing. You decide which legacy modules get modernized first, based on blast radius, data gravity and how cheaply success can be measured — not on which one looks most fun.
* Measured Reliability. You define what "reliable enough" means for each workflow: acceptance thresholds, regression suites, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, rollback paths. You know that "100% accurate" is a marketing phrase, and that the engineering version is a measured error rate with a defined containment strategy.
* The Three Things You Own
* The Guardrail Layer Input and output validation, tool-permission scoping, financial and PII data handling, sandboxed execution, human approval gates on irreversible actions, kill switches, blast-radius containment. You assume the agent will eventually do the wrong thing, and you design so that it costs us a log line instead of a General Ledger.
* The Eval Framework Golden datasets built from real ERP edge cases. Offline evals in CI as a merge gate, online evals in production. LLM-as-judge calibrated against human labels — and you know when that calibration has drifted. Regression detection when a model version, prompt or retrieval index changes underneath you. You move the squad from "prompt vibes" to a number that can fail a build.
* The Cost & Performance Envelope Model routing, caching, context budgeting, latency budgets. You track token cost per completed business transaction, not per call, and you can tell the CFO why a workflow costs what it costs and where the next 40% comes from.
* Elective Depth (be deep in one, fluent in all six)
* Agentic Architect (Systems) — state management and tool-calling interfaces for long-running business processes across complex ERP schemas.
* UX/Interaction (Product) — generative UIs and browser-use agents; designing where the human stays in the loop and where they don't need to be.
* Data & Context (Data) — RAG and knowledge-graph architecture: vector stores, chunking strategy, retrieval evals, and the relationship between a Purchase Order and a GL entry.
* Reliability & Eval (QA) — programmatic prompt optimization (DSPy), red-teaming agents, adversarial testing of financial logic.
* Infra & Agent-Ops (DevOps) — the factory where agents live: tracing, logging and monitoring the "thoughts" of the AI; deployment and rollback of prompts and models as versioned artifacts.
* Domain Logic Translation (Business) — turning 50 pages of accounting regulation into structured system prompts and agentic constraints.

**What You'll Actually Do**

* Set the definition of shippable. Write the standard for when an agent can touch production data, and enforce it in code, not in a wiki page.
* Build the eval harness and wire it into CI as a gate that can and does block merges.
* Design the guardrails around regulated and financial logic, including the human approval and rollback paths.
* Run design reviews. Kill bad agent architectures in week one instead of month four. Be specific about why.
* Own agent incidents. Pull the traces, find the root cause, and add the eval that makes that failure impossible to reintroduce.
* Make build-vs-buy calls on frameworks, vendors and models — and revisit them when the ground shifts, which it will.
* Grow Builder 1s and 2s through code review, design review and pairing. Not through ceremony.

**What Good Looks Like**
*(Targets to be agreed with the hiring manager — these are illustrative, not fixed.)*

* 90 days: Eval harness running in CI on at least two live agentic workflows, with a published reliability baseline. A written, enforced guardrail standard.
* 6 months: Every production agent has a regression suite, a cost-per-transaction number, and a rollback path. Agent-related incidents are down and post-incident evals exist for each.
* 12 months: The squad ships agentic modules on a predictable cadence without you in the critical path of each one.

**The Stack**
Python, SQL (Postgres/SQL Server), TypeScript, OpenAI/Anthropic, pgvector/Qdrant, LangChain/LangGraph, DSPy, dbt, Apache Hop/Airflow, Docker, Weights & Biases, OpenTelemetry — plus the orchestration layer you'll live in: eval and tracing platforms (LangSmith / Langfuse / Braintrust or equivalent), policy and guardrail tooling, model routing and caching. And any other tool that helps us achieve greatness.
  
  
**Who You Are**

* You've been burned. You have shipped an agentic system to real users, watched it fail in a way you didn't predict, and changed your architecture because of it. This is the single strongest signal for this level.
* Rigor over hype. You love new models and you still ask for the eval numbers first. You know the difference between a cool demo and a production-grade agent handling financial data.
* Agent-first thinker. You think in capabilities and failure modes, not functions.
* The manual-task hater. If you do a task twice, you've already started drafting the workflow that kills it.
* Technically fearless. A 500-table undocumented legacy schema is a puzzle, not a threat.
* A multiplier. Your best week is one where the squad shipped three things and you wrote one design doc and two brutal, useful reviews.

**Why Join Us**

* The Final Boss of complexity. ERPs are the hardest problem in software for AI. Automate a General Ledger and you've mastered the game.
* Agentic autonomy. We don't do tickets. We do missions. You choose the models, frameworks and architectures you believe will win.
* No red tape. If the agent works and the evals pass, we ship. No Change Management Committee — a "Does It Work?" policy. Note that you are the person who defines what "works" means.
* The Builder Tribe. You will not be the only AI person in the room. You'll lead a squad of people as obsessed with moving 10x faster as you are.

description:

:

TekWissen Group is a workforce management provider operating throughout India and several other countries worldwide. The client below is a leading technology company offering a range of IT solutions tbusinesses and organizations, enabling them ttransform their digital futures

**Job Description:**

* We are seeking a Senior Principal Engineer to build the AI-native capabilities that replace how security work is performed today.
* Security processes today run across multiple functional teams, frequently duplicated with different tooling and different definitions of done. This role re-engineers and implements the rationalized version of those processes as AI-native workflows, working from an approved solution design and directly with the teams whose work is being agentified.
* The expectation is production-grade engineering. Systems are delivered tested, instrumented so that the agent operations team can monitor them, and documented sufficiently for another engineer to extend them. Defects found in production are resolved by this role at root cause.

**Objectives of This Role**

* Cross-functional security workflows delivered as working AI-native implementations that replace the manual and fragmented processes they came from
* One implementation serving every function that shares a process, preserving in the build the consolidation the design sets out
* Delivery on committed timelines, with the reliability, observability, and cost profile to run in production
* Reusable components and patterns, so each workflow after the first starts from existing code

**Responsibilities:**

* Build the AI-native implementation of security workflows from approved solution designs, including agent loops where an agent is the right pattern, tool and service implementations, sub-agent orchestration, state and checkpoint handling, and the deterministic components that own gating and verdict logic
* Work directly with the functional owners and practitioners whose process is being agentified to establish the operational detail a solution design does not carry: real data sources, exception paths, edge cases, and current decision logic
* Re-engineer the process as part of implementing it, rather than reproducing it step for step: remove steps that exist only because the work was performed by hand, collapse handoffs and queues, and restructure sequence and timing where agentic execution changes what is possible
* Implement the consolidated workflow so that every function sharing the process is served by one build, rather than forking the implementation per team
* Implement context strategy in code: retrieval and search, memory, grounding against enterprise data sources, prompt assembly, schema-constrained output, and context budgeting under real payload sizes
* Build tool and integration surfaces against the systems each function already works in, including MCP servers, API clients, and event consumers, with scoped credentials, rate limiting, retries, backpressure, and idempotency for actions that cannot safely repeat
* Implement automated tests, validate agent behavior against the acceptance criteria defined for the workflow, and hold to code review, typed interfaces, dependency hygiene, and documentation sufficient for another engineer to extend the system
* Instrument systems for operations, providing execution traces spanning agent steps and tool calls, token and cost accounting, and latency measurement that the agent operations team can monitor against
* Engineer for cost and latency through prompt and response caching, model selection and routing with fallback, and context compaction, with measurement to confirm the effect
* Harden systems against adversarial input, including prompt injection through retrieved or user-supplied content, tool abuse, and unintended data movement through agent surfaces
* Resolve defects escalated from agent operations, including non-deterministic behavior and degradation that surfaces only under production load, fixing at root cause with regression coverage that prevents recurrence
* Validate the delivered workflow with the functional owners before release, deliver within committed windows, and raise design gaps to the solution owner rather than resolving them unilaterally in code

* Cost and latency engineering: token accounting, prompt and response caching, model routing with fallback, and context compaction
* Process re-engineering experience: analyzing an existing workflow and rebuilding it around what automation makes possible, rather than encoding current practice into software
* Experience replacing an existing manual or fragmented business process with software, working directly with the people who perform that process today
* Integration engineering: REST and GraphQL APIs, event-driven consumers, OAuth and scoped credential handling, schema and contract versioning, and resilient behavior under partial failure
* Observability and delivery engineering: structured logging, distributed tracing, and metrics for systems whose behavior varies between runs, plus CI/CD pipelines, automated quality gates, and containerized deployment
* Ability to work independently from written specification, deliver against committed timelines, and communicate progress and blockers without prompting
* Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

**Preferred Skills and Qualifications:**

* Experience building MCP servers or agent tooling, or extending AI coding assistants such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or Cursor

* Build appropriate access controls for users, internal teams, consultants, and partners.

Your work will connect mobile experiences, backend infrastructure, structured wellness data, explainable algorithms, device integrations, and operational dashboards into one integrated ecosystem.
  
  
We are looking for a technically strong, product-minded developer who is comfortable taking ownership, solving complex problems, and contributing to HiWox’s long-term vision as a founding team member.

In this role, you will be the core technical authority responsible for turning messy, fragmented, and unstructured raw data into clean, highly structured, and business-ready data assets.

You will design production-grade data preparation workflows using Alteryx Designer, leverage In-Database techniques for massive scale, enforce data quality and governance standards, and feed pristine datasets downstream to BI platforms, machine learning models, and executive reporting systems.

Key Responsibilities

Advanced Data Preparation & Cleansing

Design, build, and optimize enterprise-level Alteryx workflows dedicated to heavy data profiling, cleansing, deduplication, blending, and schema normalization from disparate, messy sources.

Standardize data inputs across structured (SQL, Snowflake), semi-structured (JSON, XML), and unstructured formats (PDFs, log files, multi-tab Excel sheets, web scrapes).

Implement advanced string manipulation, regex patterns, fuzzy matching, and parsing logic to resolve data discrepancies and unify identity records across platforms.

Architect automated data quality auditing frameworks within workflows to detect, isolate, and log missing values, schema drifts, outliers, and corrupted records before downstream consumption.

Enterprise Pipeline Development & Scalability

Build high-performance ETL/ELT data preparation pipelines utilizing Alteryx In-Database (In-Db) processing and SQL pushdown execution to process multi-terabyte datasets efficiently.

Develop reusable Batch, Iterative, and Standard Macros to standardize recurring data prep tasks (e.g., date standardization, currency conversion, schema mapping, dynamic multi-file ingestion).

Build robust error-handling, automated alerts, and logging protocols to ensure zero data loss and seamless pipeline recovery during failure events.

Manage workflow deployment, scheduling, credentials, and data connection pooling on Alteryx Server (Gallery).

Required Technical Skills

Alteryx Expertise: 5+ years of hands-on experience using Alteryx Designer with a primary focus on data preparation (Parsing, Preparation, Transform, Developer, and In-Db tool categories).

Advanced Data Wrangling: Deep mastery of data manipulation techniques—including Regex, Parse, Fuzzy Matching, Spatial Data Prep, Cross-Tab, Transpose, and Join/Union strategies.

SQL & Data Warehousing: Advanced SQL proficiency (joins, window functions, CTEs, complex data type conversions) and direct experience wrangling data within cloud warehouses (e.g., Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift).

Server Administration & Scheduling: 2+ years of experience publishing, scheduling, and optimizing memory usage for data-prep workloads on Alteryx Server.

Certifications: Alteryx Designer Advanced or Expert Certification required.

* Proven track record in managing complex data projects and leading cross-functional teams.
* Experience in working with large datasets, data warehousing, and advanced analytics tools.
* 8+ years of hands-on experience in enterprise data warehouse and data lake implementations
* 5+ years of external client consulting experience
* 5+ years of hands-on experience building automated ETL/ELT or data integration processes utilizing multiple source systems
* 5+ years of team management experience (including offshore resources)
* 5+ years of experience leading multiple external client projects simultaneously
* 5+ years of preparing detailed external client project budget estimations with strong resource management capabilities
* 3+ years of in-depth experience in architecting, designing, and implementing complex data architectures on Azure including Azure Data Factory, Azure/Managed Instance SQL Server, Azure Logic App, and Azure Synapse Analytics
* Experience mentoring teammates or conducting technical training
* Possess integrity and a strong work ethic
* Strong analytical and verbal/written communication skills

**Certifications (Preferred):**

* Certifications in BI (ETL tools, visualization tools, cloud architectures) are expected
* Certifications such as CAMS (Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist), CFE (Certified Fraud Examiner), or related data analytics certifications are a plus.

**Preferred Skills and Experience:**

* Experience working in or consulting for financial services clients is highly desirable.
* Hands-on experience with comprehensive dimensional modelling and end-to-end data warehouse projects, including:

+ Requirements gathering
+ Infrastructure planning and deployment
+ Subject matter expert interviews
+ Logical and physical dimensional model design and development
+ ETL/ELT development and maintenance model and data validation
+ Documentation

* Previous consulting experience or experience working with external clients
* Proficiency in analytics and statistical programming languages (e.g., Python, R, SQL).
* Experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) and big data technologies.
* Familiarity with machine learning frameworks and cloud-based data platforms is advantageous
* Experience working on projects using agile development practices
* Azure experience: building landing zones, provisioning resources, establishing security is a big plus

**Internal**

* Senior BI Analyst
* Data Product Manager
* BI Architect / Senior Architect
* Data Engineers
* Analytics Developers (Power BI, Tableau)

* Clients Operations Leads and Mid-Level Managers
* Data Owners, Data Stewards

The Digital CX Technology Analyst prepares and manages the data, systems and processes that power our digital customer success strategy. The role identifies, collects and prepares data, primarily from Snowflake, and enables its effective use across Gainsight CS, Gainsight PX and Journey Orchestrator. **Job Description**

**We are seeking a Principal / Lead Wireless Communications System Architect to own the definition and architectural direction of complex wireless and multi-antenna system platforms. This individual will serve as the primary technical interface with customer system teams, lead system modeling and performance analysis, drive architectural decisions across mixed-signal and digital subsystems, and define system-level specifications that translate into silicon implementations.**

**This is a senior leadership role with substantial influence across product definition, roadmap direction, and customer engagement. The ideal candidate has a deep understanding of communications theory, system decomposition across analog/digital boundaries, quantization/error propagation, MIMO signal processing architectures, and end-to-end error budgeting strategies in SDR-based environments.**

**Key Responsibilities**

**Technical Leadership and Direction: Define system architecture for next-generation multi-antenna and SDR-based communication platforms, influencing product strategy and long-term roadmap planning.**

**Customer Technical Ownership: Lead technical engagement with strategic customers, representing system trade-offs, negotiating performance specifications, and aligning joint integration plans.**

**End-to-End System Modeling: Architect and maintain MATLAB and analytical models capturing the full signal chain, including channel modeling, quantization noise allocation, SNR budgeting, interplay of RF non-linearities, and DSP algorithm design constraints.**

**Block-Level Specification Ownership: Generate precise block-level specifications for digital baseband, calibration engines, channel processing, mixed-signal converters, and RF interfacing elements; ensure internal teams understand the architectural rationale behind these specifications.**

**Cross-Domain Integration: Drive alignment between digital architecture, signal processing algorithms, mixed-signal circuit selections, ADC/DAC dynamic range decisions, LO/subsystem noise considerations, and thermal/power constraints.**

**System Verification Alignment: Collaborate with validation and silicon bring-up teams to ensure post-silicon results trace back to modeled assumptions; define measurement-level KPIs and debug methodologies when deviations arise.**

**Mentorship & Team Development: Provide architectural guidance to system engineers, signal processing developers, and hardware design teams; develop reusable models, internal best practices, and system-level methodologies.**

**Thought Leadership: Participate in internal architecture reviews, contribute to core IP innovation strategy, and represent the company in technical engagements, standards-relevant discussions, and key customer milestones.**

**Qualifications**

**Graduate degree in Electrical Engineering, Communications Engineering, or related field; PhD strongly preferred.**

**15+years of experience in wireless communications system architecture for advanced SDR systems.**

**Demonstrated ownership of end-to-end communication signal chains, including cascaded error budgeting, quantization trade-offs, and performance modeling across RF, ADC/DAC, and DSP blocks.**

**Deep Expertise In**

**MIMO and multi-user spatial processing architectures,**

**Channel estimation,**

**SNR/phase-noise budgets and their mapping into mixed-signal design requirements**

**System-level modeling using MATLAB or Python,**

**Ability to articulate complex system decisions to both internal engineering teams and senior-level customers.**

**Proven leadership in defining specifications consumed by RTL design, mixed-signal design, verification, and system validation teams.**

**Strong customer communication skills and comfort presenting architectural trade-offs to VP- and CTO-level stakeholders.**
